question: An 80-year-old man with a history of hypertension, ischemic heart disease and COPD, who underwent a complete rectocolonoscopy due to rectal bleeding, with the following findings: polypoid lesion 3 cm in diameter located 10 cm from the anal margin, occupying the half of the circumference. Rest of exploration without findings until blind. In the polyp biopsy, an adenocarcinoma limited to the submucosa is seen. Endorectal ultrasound: uT1N0. Pelvic MRI: T1N0. TC: No evidence of disease at a distance. What will be the most likely therapeutic decision to be made in the Multidisciplinary Tumor Commission?

options.opb: Neoadjuvant radiotherapy and low anterior resection of the rectum by laparoscopy.
options.opd: Anterior low resection of laparotomic rectus.
options.ope: Anterior low resection of laparoscopic rectal route and adjuvant radiotherapy.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Adenocarcinoma limited to submucosa -> uT1N0 on endorectal ultrasound -> T1N0 on pelvic MRI -> No evidence of distant disease on TC -> Therapeutic decision in Multidisciplinary Tumor Commission: Neoadjuvant radiotherapy and low anterior resection of the rectum by laparoscopy -> 85%

CHAIN: Polypoid lesion 3 cm in diameter located 10 cm from the anal margin with adenocarcinoma limited to submucosa -> uT1N0 on endorectal ultrasound -> T1N0 on pelvic MRI -> No evidence of distant disease on TC -> Therapeutic decision in Multidisciplinary Tumor Commission: Neoadjuvant radiotherapy and low anterior resection of the rectum by laparoscopy -> 80%
analysis: Based on the provided information of an 80-year-old man with a T1N0 adenocarcinoma limited to the submucosa of the rectum, the most appropriate therapeutic decision would be to proceed with a transanal endoscopic microsurgery due to the early stage of the cancer and the absence of lymph node involvement.
